title: Dichromate ion
back: Two $\ce{CrO4}$ tetrahedra sharing one O; Cr–O–Cr ≈ 126°; Cr in +6. Orange; chromate (yellow) in alkali.

title: Permanganate ion
back: Tetrahedral, Mn +7, $d^0$: purple from charge transfer, diamagnetic. Manganate ($\ce{MnO4^2-}$) is green and paramagnetic.

title: Oxidation states of the 3d metals
back: States rise to Mn (+2 to +7) and fall again; Sc only +3, Zn only +2. Steps of one, because 3d and 4s electrons are close in energy.

title: Permanganate in acid
back: Five electrons; purple → colourless, so it is its own indicator. Acidify with dilute $\ce{H2SO4}$, never HCl.

title: Chromite → potassium dichromate
back: Fuse with sodium carbonate in air, acidify, then add KCl.

title: Pyrolusite → potassium permanganate
back: Fuse to green manganate, then disproportionate in acid (or oxidise electrolytically in industry) to purple permanganate.

title: Lanthanoid contraction
back: Cause: poor shielding by 4f electrons. Results: Zr ≈ Hf in size; lanthanoids hard to separate; basicity falls La(OH)₃ → Lu(OH)₃.

title: Lanthanoids vs actinoids
back: Actinoids: more oxidation states, all radioactive, form oxo ions, stronger complexes, larger contraction.

title: A handful and an over
back: Permanganate takes 5 electrons in acid (a hand); dichromate takes 6 (a cricket over).

title: What is a transition element?
back: Incomplete d subshell in the atom or a common ion. Zn, Cd, Hg are d¹⁰ in both, so they are not transition elements.

title: Why are ions coloured?
back: Unpaired d electrons absorb visible light in d–d transitions. Sc³⁺, Ti⁴⁺, Zn²⁺, Cu⁺ are colourless; KMnO₄ is coloured by charge transfer.

title: Interstitial compounds
back: Small atoms (H, C, N) trapped in the metal lattice: very hard, high melting, conduct electricity, non-stoichiometric.

title: Transition metals as catalysts
back: They work because of variable oxidation states and a surface that adsorbs reactants.
